title: Discovery: Embeddings & Rerank - NovaCommerce
summary: Initial discovery for NovaCommerce exploring Redwood for embeddings + reranking. Customer currently using a hybrid search stack (BM25 + FAISS), evaluating model dimensionality, vector DB options, and whether to run on Hosted, Dedicated, or Private VPC. Key concerns: update latency for real-time catalog changes, throughput and cost for 10-50M vectors, and SOC2/SSO requirements. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide benchmark template and pricing, run a 1-week pilot index/bench, and schedule deep technical session with infra team.
action_items: Samira: Send pricing sheet + Dedicated capacity details by 2026-10-22
Diego: Share benchmark template and ingestion scripts (CSV + batch API) by 2026-10-21
Maya: Provide sample dataset (1M product vectors) and query profile by 2026-10-23
next_steps: Run 1-week benchmark with 10M vectors; Redwood to provide infra/benchmark template
Schedule technical deep dive (Diego + Liam) for dedicated/private deployment on 2026-10-27
Redwood to share SOC2 and SSO/KMS docs and networking runbook
transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Samira, AE at Redwood. Diego from our SE team is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Ethan (Nova): Good, thanks. Ethan here. We were excited to chat  we're re-evaluating our embeddings/rerank stack.
[00:12] Maya (Nova): Hi all, Maya. I'm the ML engineer on search.
[00:14] Liam (Nova): Liam, infra. Quick note, I might need to step out for an incident at ~30.
[00:20] Diego (Redwood SE): No worries. Quick agenda: understand current stack, workloads (QPS, vector size), update patterns, security needs, and then go over Redwood options: hosted, dedicated, private.
[00:30] Ethan: Cool. Quick background: we're an e-comm platform ~100M SKUs globally but core catalog we care about is 20M active SKUs. Currently we run BM25 in Elastic and a FAISS rerank step for embeddings for personalization.
[00:43] Maya: We use a 768-dim embedding model trained in-house but thinking of moving to a 1,024 or 1,536 model for better quality. Concern is index size and latency.
[00:55] Samira: Totally. Two quick clarifications  is your FAISS index local to each search node or a centralized service? And what's your update pattern?
[01:03] Ethan: Centralized. We reindex nightly for most of catalog, but we have streaming updates for price/stock changes that should be visible within a minute.
[01:12] Diego: Got it. So mixed batch + near-real-time updates. For refresh constraints  if you're doing minute-level updates it's relevant to our KV cache behavior and batching plumbing. We can do prefix caching to avoid re-embedding entire doc, but the vector DB/integration matters.
[01:29] Liam: Quick question: does Redwood host vectors if we choose hosted? Or do you expect us to point to our own vector DB?
[01:35] Samira: Both options. Hosted API includes storage for embeddings and Redwood manages the index (we integrate with our internal vector store). For Dedicated you can reserve GPU capacity and use Redwood-managed indices but in a private deployment we can integrate with your VPC and you can host an external vector DB.
[01:48] Maya: What about connectors? We've been looking at Pinecone and Milvus adapters.
[01:52] Diego: We have existing connectors  Pinecone, Milvus, and S3-backed batch loaders. For custom setups we provide an ingestion API so you can push vectors directly. Some teams keep FAISS on-prem and do hybrid  BM25 candidate generation then call Redwood for rerank.
[02:07] Ethan: Latency is big for us. Peak QPS is about 600 qps across regions, p99 SLA goal is <120ms for user-facing queries.
[02:16] Diego: For 600 qps you likely want Dedicated for steady throughput or Hosted with burst capacity if you want serverless. With Dedicated you can guarantee GPU allocation to keep p99 low. Our benchmarks show a 1,024-dim rerank pass (top-50 candidates) in ~30-50ms on a rtx-class pod, but numbers vary by model and batch size.
[02:37] Maya: Those sound promising. What's the cost delta vs just using FAISS on our infra?
[02:42] Samira: There's tradeoffs  self-host FAISS can be cheaper if you already own infra, but you absorb ops and complexity (sharding, failover). Redwood Dedicated adds predictable unit costs but saves engineering time. We'll share a TCO calc in the pricing sheet.
[02:56] Ethan: Another thing  dimensionality. If we move to 1,536 dims, our index size goes up ~1.5-2x, that impacts memory and throughput, right?
[03:06] Diego: Yep. For in-memory indexes doubling dims can reduce throughput and increase GPU memory. We often recommend 1,024 as a sweet spot for many production workloads. Also quantization (8-bit/4-bit) and IVF/HNSW config can shrink index size; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload.
[03:23] Maya: Are the quantization steps lossy for rerank quality? We care about small deltas in business metrics.
[03:28] Diego: Typically you see minor quality degradation with aggressive quant. We run evals on your benchmark prompt set  can flag regressions above a threshold. That's part of the pilot: measure MRR/CTR differences.
[03:38] Liam: Security checklist  SOC2, SSO, KMS for keys, network controls. Can you confirm Redwood can support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering?
[03:48] Samira: Yes. Private deployment supports VPC peering and customer KMS/HSM. Hosted supports encryption at rest and we offer KMS integrations for Dedicated. We'll attach our SOC2 report and SSO SAML flow doc.
[04:00] Ethan: Good. For vector DB integration: if we keep FAISS, we'd like to avoid double indexing. Can Redwood call out-of-process FAISS for rerank to avoid moving data?
[04:10] Diego: You can do hybridgenerate candidates in Elastic/FAISS and call Redwood for re-scoring only. We support a simple top-K scoring API to send candidate ids + vectors or just vectors. If you want our Hosted index to be the source of truth we can ingest from your pipeline, but streaming small updates is supported via the batch API.
[04:29] Maya: On ingestion velocity  our streaming updates might be ~200 updates/sec during peak. How does Redwood handle that?
[04:36] Diego: For streaming rates like 200/s we recommend batching in small windows (1-5 seconds) and using our ingestion API with backpressure. Dedicated deployments can sustain higher ingest throughput. We'll include sample batching code.
[04:48] Ethan: Any constraints on vector dimensionality we should be aware of? Like max dims?
[04:53] Samira: No hard max, but practical limits apply per index type  memory & latency tradeoffs. We routinely handle up to 2,048 dims, but recommend evaluating quality vs cost during the pilot.
[05:04] Maya: Regarding hybrid search, what's the recommended flow? BM25 for recall, embeddings for personalization, then rerank with a cross-encoder?
[05:12] Diego: Exactly. Typical pattern: BM25 candidate generation -> vector similarity (embed) rerank for personalization -> optional cross-encoder or LTR model for final ranking. Redwood supports both similarity-based rerank and model-based scoring if you want to host a small cross-encoder on inference pods.
[05:26] Maya: Do you support on-device cross-encoder scoring within the same pod? We want to keep latency under 120ms at p99.
[05:33] Diego: Yes, we can co-locate cross-encoders; latency depends on model size. Small cross-encoders are fine; larger ones will push p99. We'll run candidate-size experiments  top-20 vs top-50  to find sweet spot.
[05:45] Ethan: About durability  if we use Hosted, what retention and backup policies exist for vector data?
[05:50] Samira: Hosted includes snapshots/backups and retention policies; Dedicated provides configurable retention, and Private you control retention. We'll include the retention SLAs in the doc.
[05:59] Liam: Networking specifics for Private: do you support VPC peering across accounts and private endpoints? We have strict egress rules.
[06:06] Diego: Yes, VPC peering and private endpoints are supported. We have a networking runbook that details routing, NAT, and firewall rules. We'll share that.
[06:15] Ethan: Can Redwood run an existing model we have (1,024-dim custom model), or do you require using your catalog?
[06:21] Samira: You can bring-your-own-model for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can also host custom modelsrequires model vetting and a small onboarding. Diego can follow up on the model packaging steps.
[06:31] Diego: Quick note on benchmarking  to get good apples-to-apples numbers we need: a) sample vectors, b) query distribution, c) candidate sizes. We'll produce a benchmark harness that runs vector similarity and rerank pass and reports p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization.
[06:45] Maya: That would be great. Also, do you have examples of index sizes per dim for guidance?
[06:50] Diego: We'll include a sizing table in the benchmark doc (e.g., 10M x 768 ~ X GB; 10M x 1024 ~ Y GB)  rough numbers depend on quantization and index type (HNSW vs IVF).
[07:00] Ethan: On cost, we care about per-query unit economics. Can Redwood provide tokenized cost for rerank ops?
[07:06] Samira: We'll include per-rerank cost estimates based on candidate size, model choice, and quantization profile. Also show TCO vs self-host FAISS across scenarios.
[07:16] Maya: Any limitation for cross-region queries? We have users in EU and NA.
[07:21] Diego: We support region routing and multi-region deployment. For p99 SLOs we recommend colocating indices or using regional Dedicated pools. We can configure smart routing policies.
[07:33] Liam: SLA terms for Dedicated  what's uptime and latency guarantees?
[07:37] Samira: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime (99.9% typically) and latency SLOs based on reserved capacity. We'll include specific SLA language in the enterprise packet.
[07:48] Ethan: Data residency  some EU data must stay in EU. Can you pin indexing and storage to a region for Hosted?
[07:55] Samira: Yes, region pinning is supported for Hosted and required for Private. We'll detail region options in the doc.
[08:04] Maya: For the pilot, we're thinking 1-week run with 10M vectors and typical query load. Does Redwood charge for pilot?
[08:11] Samira: We usually offer a limited free pilot for evaluation; for larger pilots (10M+ vectors + heavy QPS) we talk pilot credits/discounts. We'll outline options in pricing.
[08:21] Ethan: Sounds good. A few nitty-gritty things  how do you handle preservation of metadata and ability to rehydrate vectors if we need to rebuild index?
[08:30] Diego: We support storing raw vectors + metadata as part of the index and snapshots for rehydration. For very large sets we recommend incremental snapshots to S3 for faster restores.
[08:40] Maya: One more question  can we run custom similarity functions or binary pipelines? For example, a weighted dot-product mixing dense and sparse features?
[08:48] Diego: We support hybrid scoring; you can provide weighted features and call a rerank model. Some advanced custom scoring may require a SE integration but is typically supported in Dedicated/Private modes.
[09:00] Ethan: Any limits on candidate size for rerank? For instance our current flow sometimes does top-200 from BM25 then rerank.
[09:07] Diego: Top-200 is doable but will increase latency. Most customers find top-20/50+cross-encoder is best tradeoff. We'll trial different top-K sizes in the benchmark.
[09:18] Samira: Quick recap  Redwood will: share pricing + TCO, SOC2 and SSO/KMS docs, benchmark template and ingestion scripts, and schedule a technical deep dive. Nova to share sample dataset and query profile.
[09:31] Maya: Yep. I'll package a 1M sample and query logs anonymized.
[09:34] Ethan: Also want to loop in our product lead for business-metric acceptance criteria during pilot.
[09:39] Samira: Great, add them to the calendar invite for the deep dive.
[09:42] Liam: Sorry I need to run now  but I'll be on the deep dive. Thanks.
[09:46] Diego: Thanks Liam. We'll follow up via email with attachments  deck links, benchmark harness, and sample sizing table (tinyurl.com/rw-embeddings-bench).
[09:56] Ethan: Quick clarification  when you say \"Hosted stores vectors\", what's the encryption model?
[10:00] Samira: Encryption at rest and in transit; for Hosted we manage keys unless you opt for customer KMS for Dedicated or Private. We'll send the KMS integration doc.
[10:10] Maya: Anything else?
[10:12] Samira: That's it from us. Thanks everyone  we'll follow up with the action items.
[10:16] Ethan: Thanks, bye.
[10:18] Diego: Bye.
